chunks: O my two fellow prisoners, as for one of you, he will give his master wine to drink, and as for the other, he will be crucified, and the birds will eat from his head. The matter concerning which you ask is already decided.
ai.seo_question: What did Joseph predict for his two fellow prisoners in the Quran?
ai.summary: In this verse, Prophet Joseph (AS) interprets the dreams of his fellow prisoners, predicting one will serve wine to the Pharaoh and the other will be crucified with birds eating from his head. The phrase 'Qudiya al-amr' (the matter has been decreed) highlights the certainty of divine fate, a concept often emphasized in Shia exegesis to illustrate the transition from human inquiry to divine resolution. This interpretation serves as a precursor to Joseph's eventual rise to power, linking personal destiny to broader divine plans.
